headline: Paper finds asynchronous delivery order can change search agents’ acquired evidence and proposes schedule-stable coordination
summary: A preprint reports that changing the delivery order of identical evidence packets can alter what search agents retrieve, with the difference persisting after all initial evidence arrives and through another search. Across controlled QA tasks, early commitment produced 11.6–23.8 percentage points of acquisition disagreement above same-order repeat variation in eight model-task settings. The paper proposes Confluent Evidence Acquisition (CEA), which waits for each subquestion’s assigned evidence and uses a schedule-independent rule to allocate shared searches. In question-only plans, the authors report acquisition disagreement near repeat variation across three benchmarks; accuracy was comparable to a complete-input control and improved over early commitment on 2Wiki and HotpotQA, but not MuSiQue. These are author-reported results in a frozen-corpus QA setting, not an independently reproduced finding or a demonstration across deployed agents.
